source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
For the sensor board, it has two input connectors coming from the main board — one 4-pin JST-PH 2.0mm for power (5V, GND, 3V3, GND) and one 6-pin JST-GH 1.25mm for signals (SDA0, SCL0, SDA1, SCL1, UART TX, UART RX).
Then it has output connectors going to each sensor module:

\- SCD41 — 4-pin JST-GH (3V3/GND/SDA0/SCL0)
\- BME280 — 4-pin JST-GH
\- ENS160 — 4-pin JST-GH
\- SPS30 — 5-pin JST-ZH 1.5mm (5V, SDA0, SCL0, SEL→GND, GND) — different connector type, matches SPS30 cable
\- ZE08-CH2O — 7-pin JST-GH (matches supplied cable)
\- I2C display — 4-pin JST-GH (3V3/GND/SDA1/SCL1)
\- One spare I2C0 port — 4-pin JST-GH
\- One spare I2C1 port — 4-pin JST-GH

So 10 connectors total. Full pinouts are in the sensor board doc.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: one thing just we need to make sure, is SPS30 pin 4 (SEL) hardwired to GND on the PCB? This is critical, if SEL floats or goes HIGH, the SPS30 switches to UART mode and won't respond on I2C

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: In the pdf file I sent you, SEL is connected to gnd
